Text: Labourers in {StarSystem} have unearthed ancient holographic projectors
These devices once projected 3D images across {StarSystem}’s station; this cluster was part of an entertainment complex. They’re in poor repair; who knows what holo-programs they once rendered?
Available from your house's action list
The projectors can be refitted for military or engineering purposes.
The holographic projectors have been repaired
{D(Tech)} has a few ideas regarding how to use them.
Create the illusion of impenetrable defences on {StarSystem}
While the holograms could have briefly fooled an attacking fleet, the ruse is now public knowledge.
The ruse will be discovered after {StarSystem} is attacked.
Holographic projections give {StarSystem} the appearance of formidable defences. If attacked, however, the illusion will be broken.
Use them to create illusory ships during battle
By using holograms to create duplicates of their ships, {House} gains an edge in battle.
Use 3D light grids as engineering guides
The use of holographic guidelines during construction projects improves {House}'s engineering accuracy.

You can repair your holographic projectors.

More holographic devices have been discovered in {StarSystem}

Based on their distribution, there was a network of holograms throughout the station. Your technicians have recovered damaged memory files referring to a “Space Park”: some kind of entertainment venue they were part of, centuries ago.

We could repurpose these devices, though the repairs would be costly.
Salvage the devices and install them in {HomeSystem}
The projector network has been relocated

The devices need to be repaired, and programmed with a new holo-program of our own making.

“Well,” {Tech} muses, “what message from {PlayerHouse} should my technicians fashion? What is so unique about our House that we’d put it up in lights?”

The holographic network has been repaired

Holograms appear across {StarSystem}, “helping our subjects understand our deepest values”. After a few weeks, no denizen of {StarSystem} can escape the flood of pro-{PlayerHouse} propaganda.

Hearing these holograms on an hourly basis is a small, if irritating, price to pay.
{D(Nice)} questioned the ethics of your hologram network

“I’ve met a number of commoners obsessed with our holo-programs. They hum the songs, or greet the holo-effigies like bosom friends. One man dreams of them every night. Is it right to warp their minds for the sake of our pride?”
{D(Nasty)} scoffs. “Is it our fault these weak-willed cattle can’t tell reality from fantasy?”
{Nice} is right: we shouldn’t abuse our people
Popular support is too valuable: the holograms stay

“The holographic network is deteriorating,” {Tech} cries. “They’ve reverted to their original programs: advertisements and jingles for some... holiday destination?” Suddenly, a 100-foot-high figure materialises on the station’s promenade. “Space is the place to chase... your dreams,” it intones, with a look of wonder. {StarSystem}’s people are going to love hearing that on the hour, every hour. {StarSystem} will gain +4 unrest per turn until the problem is fixed.

The assignee's <helptext>tech</helptext> is tested.
- Pass: the holographic network is repaired
- Fail: the holographic network is destroyed

“Let’s see if we can shut these mascots up for good,” {he(Assignee)} grins, throwing the switch.

The Space Park advertisements wink out.

You breathe a sigh of relief, making a mental note to thank {d(Assignee)} later - and to expunge the phrase “Space is the place” from your memory.

“Let’s see if we can shut these mascots up for good,” {he(Assignee)} grins, throwing the switch.

The Space Park advertisements wink out.

When the holograms re-engage, they show a gigantic Earth-mammal touting a sign the size of a frigate. “Is that a rabbit?” {d(Assignee)} squints. “Or... were they called ‘hamsters’?” The creature opens its smiling maw. The entire facility rocks as it bellows: “Now only four ninety nine ninety nine!” “I don’t care what it is,” you shout, “or what it thinks it’s selling: shut it down!”
The mascot holograms have been disabled

It took three long, sleepless nights, but the bellowing mammal is finally silent. 

Everyone agrees, without reservation, that ripping out the entire holographic network was a very small price to pay.
Technicians on this system were unable to fix temperamental holograms.
